gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have booked — the hotel had plenty of rooms left.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' shows an unnecessary completed action: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: Nobody ___ have predicted that result — it shocked everyone.
gaps.hint: it was impossible at that time
gaps.explanation: 'Could have' in negatives means it was not possible: could have predicted.

gaps.sentence: You ___ told me — I would have kept the evening free!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' plus the participle criticizes something that did not happen: should have told.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be at work — I've just seen him at the beach.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses something the evidence rules out.

gaps.sentence: You ___ touch that wire — it carries a live current!
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' signals something absolutely not allowed: mustn't touch.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to be more careful with your passwords.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' behaves like 'should' and always takes 'to': ought to be.

gaps.sentence: The theatre was completely empty, so the performance ___ have been very popular.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' draws a negative conclusion from evidence: can't have been.
